title: Median product "lifespan" has fallen from ~4y down to ~1.5y
selftext:
The "product graveyard" of SaaSHub has been tracking the status (and lifespan) of hundreds of thousands of products. It's been hovering around 4y for quite some time. However, there's a sharp decline in 2026 leading to about 1.5y these days. https://www.saashub.com/product-graveyard That's a huge drop. And, it matches my "human" observations. A lot of products are being vibe coded, released, and soon after that abandoned. It's become too cheap to produce software. So, a lot of people have been experimenting for 'free' with their ideas - only to find out that they weren't viable... or that they couldn't bring customers in. Distribution and marketing have become much more important than before - within the context that everyone can build "features" for free.

Anyhow, I expect this trend of shortening product lifespan to continue even further down. Or maybe, at some point people will realised that there are no users for their products as every user can "build" their own and custom product. Leaving us with a dozen huge platforms that host and help you build those apps. Until then - it's a crazy gold rush and a lot of makers are abandoning their empty buckets.

title: Ask HN: Is it not possible to enroll for Apple Developer anymore?
selftext:
I've been trying to enroll for Apple Developer for over a month and nothing works.

The Apple Developer app won't accept my Canadian passport for identity verification. The enrollment is for a Delaware LLC, so my Apple account region is set to US. I can't switch the account region to Canada either, because I haven't lived there in years and don't have a Canadian bank card.

If I enroll through the website, the enrollment gets approved, I accept the term and, when it's time to pay, all my cards get declined. I tried ~7 bank cards (debit, credit, personal, business), all with matching billing addresses. All US cards. All the banks tell me they didn't decline transactions from Apple. I tried no VPN, VPN and residential VPN. I tried from my MacBook, iPhone, Safari, Chrome, incognito, non-incognito.

Phone support is unavailable every time I check. I tried talking to regular Apple Store customer support but after repeating myself over 5 times with different agents, the last person I got transferred to told me they couldn't help with Developer stuff.

If I email Developer support, they reply ~5 days later with unhelpful canned responses like "have you tried Safari incognito?", "you should try the Developer app instead" or "make sure your billing address matches your bank information". I'm at support email #9 and enrollment attempt #3.

Has anyone had similar issues and been able to fix them?
author: olalonde

title: Open-source, cross-harness memory for AI agents
selftext:
Earlier this year, my co-founder and I found ourselves frequently switching between different coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) anytime we ran out of shaky usage limits or a newer, better model came out.

We became increasingly frustrated with having to re-explain our tasks, workflows, common mistake patterns, etc. anytime we switched agents. We found no good free alternatives out there, so we built our own and fully open-sourced it!

Beacon hooks into 20+ different agent harnesses, captures session telemetry (prompts, tool calls, command executions, etc) in one normalized format, and distills it into common patterns and repeatable workflows with a human-approval step. This compounded knowledge is then accessible to any future agent via skills / MCP.

We believe your agent data is yours to own and should not be locked behind any frontier lab's ecosystem or closed memory infrastructure. We built Beacon to make working across agents way more transparent and efficient.

Try it out and tell us what you think: https://github.com/Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon

title: RSC and CDN interaction makes next.js inefficient for highload projects
selftext: ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/rsc-test-m43xq4 ### To Reproduce 1. Build the application next build 2. Start the application next start 3. Navigate to category 1 4. Navigate to category 2 with hard refresh ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current Behavior** Product 1 appears in category 1 and category 2 Currently they return return identical data, but have a different `rsc` hash **Expected Behaviour** If the data is the same there should be only one `rsc` hash. With a high throughput global ecommerce site I want to cache identical data close to the customer in a CDN. The different `rsc` hashes mean that I will get CDN cache misses and traffic will have to go back to the server, potentially a distance from the customer and with a slower response time. ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 23.4.0: Fri Mar 15 00:10:42 PDT 2024; root:xnu-10063.101.17~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 Available memory (MB): 65536 Available CPU cores: 10 Binaries: Node: 18.18.0 npm: 10.1.0 Yarn: 1.22.19 pnpm: N/A Relevant Packages: next: 14.2.3 // Latest available version is detected (14.2.3). eslint-config-next: 14.1.0 react: 18.3.1 react-dom: 18.3.1 typescript: 5.4.5 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Performance ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) next start (local) ### Additional context Hi I'm trying to work out how I make the RSC requests work with a CDN when self hosting Nextjs. Is there any more info on this subject. I'm working on an ecommerce site with 100,000 products. Those products could appear in numerous product listing pages (search result pages). Each of those PLP pages are given unique URLs for SEO purposes. Take for example the following URLs: /mens/ /mens/trainers /mens/trainers/brand /mens/trainers/brand?facet-price=%3A168 They could all have the same products in. Due to the way the rsc hash is calculated that means I get a different _rsc params on each listing page, even though the contents of that response is exactly the same. product/299336/?_rsc=1vl30 product/299336/?_rsc=qe3go product/299336/?_rsc=1vg99 product/299336/?_rsc=1stsw I have even gone to different areas of the site cart, checkout, order history, all with links back to the same product, they each produce different _rsc params, but still the data returned is identical? On a high throughput site I want to be able to cache identical data in the CDN close to the customer. At the moment that would be impossible as there would be to many variations on the rsc hash to make the caching effective. For solutions I think I only have 2 options: Cache all rsc requests in the CDN - this would end up caching loads of duplicate data and get cache misses when they should be hits Pass all request through to the Nextjs server. - With this solution I would worry the server would be overloaded at peak periods. In both cases there would be an extra cost to the client I'm trying to understand why the rsc has is different when it is always returning identical data? What is the purpose of this hash? As mentioned before could this just be set to _rsc=1? We would also have issues with the Vary header as it is currently returned like this: Vary: RSC, Next-Router-State-Tree, Next-Router-Prefetch, Next-Url In this case the Next-Router-State-Tree and Next-Url will be set on where you are coming from and do not necessarily have an impact on the data need for the page we are going to. The Vary header will again have an impact on the CDN This issue has been rasied in the following discussion thread https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/59167 [NEXT-3327](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/NEXT-3327/rsc-and-cdn-interaction-makes-nextjs-inefficient-for-highload-projects)

selftext:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

### To Reproduce

First serve it in dev mode to see how it should work
1. copy .env.example and set credentials (or leave them as is)
2. run mongodb via docker `docker-compose up`
3. run next.js app via `npm run nx serve next-broken`
4. IN browser see how it shows proper model name `BrokenModel`

Now build app and run it in prod mode
1. build the app with `npm run nx build next-broken`
2. serve it with `npm run nx run next-broken:serve:production`
3. open browser or check the terminal of the IDE
4. model name becomes `p` while it should still be `BrokenModel`


### Current vs. Expected behavior

I'd expect model names (based on class name) to not be minified as it breaks typegoose.

It breaks since next 14
If I disable minification in `next.conif.js`
```
webpack: (config) => {
    config.optimization.minimize = false;
    return config;

```

Then it works, but the build is not optimized which is not acceptable for prod.

As a workaround I could use `TerserPlugin` and set `keep_classnames: true` and then it works fine. (see with-terser` branch in github repo.
But it would be nice to get an official guideline.

selftext: For the biggest tech company this side of the Sun, it’s clunky, unreliable, not nearly as smooth and intuitive as gTasks, and I simply don’t like it.

title: Longtime user frustrated by iOS version
selftext:
I’ve used Google Tasks for 10+ years, multiple times a day, with 30–40 lists containing everything from daily tasks to personal notes, memories, work information, and even detailed lists of what’s in my storage bins. It’s become an important personal reference system.

After switching from Android to iPhone about a year ago, I’ve been extremely frustrated by how limited the iOS version is compared with Android. And now, in the latest update, a particularly useful feature appears to have been removed: the drop-down menu in the upper-left corner that let you quickly see and select from all your lists.

With dozens of lists, having to scroll horizontally through them is significantly slower and more cumbersome. I genuinely don’t understand why such a basic and useful feature would be removed.

Please bring it back—and please give the iOS version the same functionality as Android. Longtime users like me depend on this app, and it’s frustrating to see it become less useful over time. I’m now being forced to look for something different. Ugg!
